@graph.name: Trip Interruption
@graph.description: Travel Guard’s Trip Interruption provides coverage for your vacation in case an unforeseen, covered event sends you home early.

acceptedAnswer.text: Trip Interruption coverage begins when you start your trip. It provides protection for your travel investment if a covered reason causes you to miss a portion of the trip or stop the trip completely and return home early. Trip Interruption can reimburse you for parts of your trip that you miss, as well as additional transportation costs incurred to continue the trip or return home.

mainEntity.name: How do I use the Trip Interruption benefit if my trip gets interrupted?

acceptedAnswer.text: When your trip is cut short or you face a significant delay, you can make any changes to your trip directly through your travel suppliers, such as the airline or cruise you booked with originally. If you need additional help making new reservations or booking transportation, our 24/7 emergency travel assistance team can help you at 800.826.5248. Once your travels are complete and you’ve returned home, you can submit your claim with the required documentation and request to be reimbursed for any covered expenses.

mainEntity.name: What documentation do I need to file my claim?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The specific documentation needed for your Trip Interruption claim will depend on the reason for interruption and what expenses you incurred. Listed below are examples of documentation that may be required.

- Travel Guard claim form

- Documentation to support the reason for the interruption to your trip

- Proof of travel/reservations

- Incident reports

- Receipts for any claimed expenses

- Medical reports, invoices and receipts

There may be additional documents required based on your specific claim. You can start the process of filing a claim online with our claims portal or you can call us directly if you have specific questions.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Trip Interruption and Trip Cancellation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest difference between these benefits is when the coverage is provided. Trip Cancellation provides coverage from the day after you purchase the travel insurance plan, until departure. Trip Interruption provides coverage once your trip starts up until you arrive back home. For more information, be sure to review your travel insurance plan details.

mainEntity.name: What is Trip Interruption – Return Transportation Only?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes you score an amazing deal on flights, which is great! Until you need to travel home in the middle of your trip unexpectedly. Because the standard Trip Interruption benefit limits are typically a percentage of your original trip cost, that might not leave you with enough coverage for your last-minute flight home. Trip Interruption – Return Transportation Only can help in this situation. Rather than a percentage, the benefit offers a flat amount of coverage to file a claim against (typically between $500 and $1,000). The two Trip Interruption coverages can’t be combined, and our Travel Guard team can help you figure out which option works best for you.

mainEntity.name: Is Trip Interruption coverage worth it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! While a travel insurance plan may seem like just another expense up front, coverages like Trip Interruption can offer extra peace of mind, providing protection for your travel investment and the extra unexpected costs associated with ending your trip early.

mainEntity.name: Can I purchase Trip Interruption coverage at any time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trip Interruption coverage comes as part of the standard coverages on most Travel Guard travel insurance plans. You can purchase a travel insurance plan to cover your trip up until the day before your departure. However, it should be noted that a loss must be considered “unforeseen” for coverage to apply, so waiting to buy a plan until you know something will interrupt your trip will not help. It’s best to get the protection in place early.

mainEntity.name: What is considered a covered reason to end my trip early under Trip Interruption?

acceptedAnswer.text: Situations that are covered under Trip Interruption are unforeseen events and circumstances that leave you unable to continue your travels. For example, Sickness or Injury to yourself, a Traveling Companion or family member may qualify you for coverage. Other events like severe weather or natural disasters may lead to a covered reason to interrupt a trip as well. A complete list of covered reasons and exclusions can be found in your policy of insurance.
